articleTitle: Development of a Master-Slave Robotic System for Vascular Interventional Surgery
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Robot-assisted vascular interventional surgery (VIS) can effectively reduce the surgeon’s exposure to X-ray radiation. However, some existing robotic system cannot meet the surgical requirements for rapidly exchanging catheter/guidewire or lack force detection. These would waste patients’ valuable treatment time and increase the system’s insecurity. This paper presents a developed master–slave vascular intervention robotic system. It allows for quick catheter/guidewire installation and has force feedback. This paper analyzes the structure of force measurement on the slave side. Different axial force accuracies are obtained by selecting two flexible materials for the axial force calibration part. The results show that the influence of the flexible material on the accuracy of the axial force plays an important role. In addition, the stability of the system’s axial force measurement is verified through the endo vascular evaluator (EVE) model experiment. Finally, the effects of material and axial force accuracy are discussed. The system developed in this paper will make a certain contribution to the development of a master–slave robotic system for VIS.

articleTitle: Implementation of Reservoir Computing Algorithm in Stretchable Sensor for Wearable Device
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Hand gesture is one example of a communication method for people with a hearing disorder. Currently, researchers have developed the stretchable sensing that is based on soft materials for supporting the devices of the conveys messages. Consequently, the real-time response and accuracy of the device are the major issue in the development process. However, the signal classification of soft sensors is still not widely used as a recognitive tool for human movement. In this current study, we applied the machine learning to understand and classify the human movement sign. This research presented the classification of the signal of the hand gesture language by using the reservoir computing algorithm. We expect that our reservoir computing model will classify the stretchable sensor sign. The results of the reservoir computing implementation classified the three signals of the hand languages. The reservoir computing’s performance showed that the weight input (W<inf>in</inf>) is the essential feature of the learning parameter. The significant parameters of reservoir computing support the optimizing performance of the classification.

articleTitle: Fabrication of a stretchable electroadhesive pad
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Electrostatic adhesion technology has recently attracted much attention for use in the field of soft robotics for wall walking and grasping complex-shaped objects. In the development of soft robots using electrostatic adhesion technology, it is critical to simplify the manufacturing process and to optimize the electrode shape. A previous study employed a conductive silicone rubber sheet to simplify the manufacturing process. Electrolytic analysis indicated that the optimum electrode shape is a wave. Referring to these previous studies, we manufactured an electroadhesive pad with wave-shaped electrodes using a highly efficient method. An electroadhesive pad was completed in 90 minutes. The resulting electroadhesive pad showed that the shear pressure increased in proportion to the square of the voltage, which is consistent with theory. Our technology should contribute to the mass production of electroadhesive pads and increase the manufacturing efficiency of soft robots that can walk on walls and grasp objects with complex shapes.

articleTitle: Cyborg Cockroaches can be Commanded to Play Soccer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Nowadays, cyborg insects are used for various applications such as search and rescue operations, environmental monitoring, and many others. However, the cyborg insect for entertainment purposes is quite new. Therefore, this study implements Madagascar Hissing Cockroach (MHC) as a cyborg insect platform for playing game purpose. A small size electronic backpack that can transmit IMU data and receive stimulation commands from a computer was developed. User Interface (UI) is developed for an efficient interface between a computer, human operator, and cyborg insects. A wireless gamepad is applied to provide the stimulation command from the human operator to the electronic backpack attached to the cockroach. The experimental result showed that the two cyborg cockroaches could be utilized for the entertainment purpose of playing soccer with a table tennis ball. Our experimental study successfully implemented cyborg cockroaches in the entertainment application.

articleTitle: Control Method of Fabric Actuator Suit for Gaze Guidance in Immersive Spaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing demand for teleoperation in immersive spaces. Users wear a head-mounted display in the immersive spaces to obtain visual information from all directions. However, they often lose sight of the target object owing to the large amount of obtained visual information. Therefore, this study proposes a novel system to physically guide a user’s gaze without using visual information by using a fabric actuator suit. A fitting algorithm is implemented in the proposed system for the fabric actuator suit along with a pressure control method for the actuator and subject experiments are conducted to verify the physical gaze guidance.

articleTitle: Intension Reading based Task Outcome Prediction for Operability Improvement of Time-Delayed Teleoperation System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we propose an intention reading system that mitigates the time-delay effect to make teleoperated robots more practical. This system reads operator’s intention by showing a near future of operator’s outcome which is predicted based on a physical model. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated through a pouring task which is to pour a predetermined amount of steel balls into the cup. The proposed system improves the accuracy of the poured amount of steel balls even in the condition of having relatively long communicational latency.

articleTitle: Display and Disposal Work Using an Electromagnet Hand and Magnetic Markers
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Product display using a electromagnets hand and a magnetic marker is proposed. The electromagnet marker places two magnets on left and right side of the QR code. The two magnets are arranged with reversed S-N poles and are attached to the front and rear surfaces of the product so that the magnets are attracted in the correct combination when the product is aligned. The magnetic markers are also attached to the top surface of the product for gripping from the top surface, and only QR codes for posture recognition are attached to the left and right sides of the product. By using magnetic markers, magnets are attracted to each other when displaying on the shelf, enabling accurate align from the front stopper on the display. In addition, the attraction of the magnets has the advantage of making the markers more robust to positioning errors during product grasping and display. The three main movements of grasping a product using an electromagnet hand are: pick-and-place operation by grasping the electromagnet marker on the top surface of the product, turning to the standing position when it has lain, and reversing the holding posture from front to back corresponding to the workspace of the manipulator. Manipulation motion for the product with magnetic markers using the proposed electromagnet hand were implemented to the 6DOF robot arm UR-5 to confirm its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Welding seam detection between cylinder and plane using point cloud data
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Welding seam detection method for cylinder and plane using point clouds is proposed. Steel used for welding is generally covered with mill scale on its surface, and its color is black so that the image processing is difficult. Furthermore, the measured point cloud with an angle has many measurement errors. In the proposed method, the point clouds are acquired separately at an angle to capture the plane and the side of the cylinder perpendicularly to reduce noise in the depth sensor. The spatial equation of the plane is derived from the point cloud data of the plane, and the centerline and radius of the cylinder are derived from the point cloud of the cylinder’s side by fitting the cylinder model. The welding line between the cylinder and the plane is derived by an ideal intersection line from the models of the plane and the cylinder. Experimental results using the proposed method show that the welding line can be obtained with good accuracy.

articleTitle: Driving of flagellated micro-gel robot by using light-scanning system
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We propose a micro-gel robot which has a flagellar-like structure. An actuator of microrobot is made of a thermoresponsive hydrogel, and we mix the actuator with CNTs so that we can drive them by irradiating light. We designed microrobots considering Reynolds number and fabricated them. Moreover, we actuated microrobots and succeeded in driving them and realizing a propulsion.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Method to Extend a 2-Dimensional Gait to 3-Dimensions in a Human Musculoskeletal Model with 70 Muscles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, to understand the mechanism of human gait, we applied the 2-dimensional gait to a human musculoskeletal model with 70 muscles, and investigated the extension method to 3-dimensional gait. We tested 4 optimization conditions to achieve a 14 degrees of freedom 3-dimensional gait using a musculoskeletal model with 70 muscles, and verified whether the model could achieve gait or not. As a result, gait was achieved only under condition 4, in which the DOFs were added step by step in the frontal axis, vertical axis, and then in the sagittal axis at each joint. The optimization procedure for condition 4 resulted in a 5-second gait. However, the results differed from those of the subject experiments in terms of stride length, average gait speed, and ankle joint angular change, and we discussed points that should be considered in the future. In the future, we would like to reproduce 3-dimensional gait, taking into consideration the points mentioned in the discussion, and contribute to the understanding of the mechanism of human gait.

articleTitle: Knee joint angle estimation by sequential correction of gyroscope bias
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: For the estimation of the knee joint angle during walking in this study, a Kalman filter is devised to sequentially correct the bias error of the gyroscope and the output of the accelerometer. Human locomotion is produced by the rotational motion of the respective joints, causing the proportion of the centrifugal acceleration and the tangential acceleration in a part of the body to increase during exercise. Thus, the proposed method considers the centrifugal and tangential acceleration to correct the accelerometer output. During a laboratory experiment, the knee joint angles of four participants are measured using an optical 3D motion analysis system and two nineaxis motion sensors while the participants were walking. The accuracy of the proposed method is verified by comparing the results obtained by the proposed sensor fusion and those obtained with an optical 3D motion analysis system.

articleTitle: Automatic Puncture Needle Detection by Image Processing Using Deep Learning and CT Values
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, a needle detection method in CT image for robotized Interventional Radiology (IR) is proposed. There are two stage to detect the needle form. First, the set of 32 square pixels including the needle is abstracts using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). In second stage, pixel-wised form is picked up based on the algorithm to compare CT value on a pixel with its surrounding pixels. 346 sets of CT images were used to train the learner, the evaluation, and evaluate the detection. Finally proposed effectiveness of algorithm is confirmed with simulation.

articleTitle: Rearrangement planning with multi-functional shelf considering the cost of regrasping products and changing posture of products
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: By providing store shelves with the ability to manage the stock and expiration dates of products on the shelves, it will be possible to plan the timing of product replenishment. Furthermore, the display, disposal, and replenishment of products can be automated by combining a robot manipulation function. The display, disposal, and replenishment require an optimal movement according to the state of the products on shelves. If the robot approaches the shelf and checks the position/status of the products, it is difficult to have enough time to calculate an optimized rearrangement plan. Therefore, if the rearrangement of products is planned by the shelf and the planning is completed before the robot arrives on the shelf, the robot will be able to perform the optimal operation quickly. In this paper, the movement cost is considered so that the movement distance of the products is minimized. Furthermore, we implement a display and disposal plan that takes into account the regrasping motion and product pose changing which is required corresponding to the manipulator’s workspace to change the location where the product is grasped, so that the product can be placed in the final display posture.

articleTitle: Lift-off Process of On-chip Micro-Gel Actuator for Cell Manipulations
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a lift-off process of a hydrogel actuator to realize large movement of them to designed direction. We patterned dextran as a sacrificial layer to lift off hydrogel actuators. By constraint one side of gel actuators, we can deform them to one direction without constraint. As an application of the process, we fabricated gel actuators with needle to stimulate microorganisms.

articleTitle: Ring-shaped wearable device for logging finger usage in daily life
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: To verify the feasibility of rehabilitation inter-vention, quantitative assessment by comparing the rate of paralyzed limb usage in daily activities between before and after an intervention is crucial. However, questionnaires and/or interview-based assessments are generally used for the purpose in most of the rehabilitation hospitals. For this aim, we developed a ring-shaped wearable device for logging hand and finger usage in daily life. Twelve participants took part in the experiments to validate the proposed device. We firstly conducted the experiment to evaluate the finger angle estimation ability of the device. Second, we observed the accumulated values of finger angle difference and wrist acceleration under six distinct upper extremity tasks in daily living, and then investigated the relationship between sensor values and behaviors. First experiment demonstrated that the device realized accurate finger angle estimation (mean absolute error was 3.34± 1.54deg) compared with previous studies. Moreover, the second experiment revealed that the device has the ability to discriminate various daily behaviors, e.g., wiping a table and folding a handkerchief (p<0.01). These results suggest that the proposed device is helpful for the medical doctors and therapists to understand recovery status of the patients.

articleTitle: Heat Source Approaching by Cyborg Cockroach Using a New Antennae Electrode Implantation Method
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Cyborg insects consist of an insect and an electronic backpack. The insect and the backpack are connected by electrodes, which can control the insect’s movement through electrical stimulation. Insects have many actuators and sensors in their small bodies and are expected to operate in confined spaces such as in rubble. Because they are small, several cyborgs are expected to be used simultaneously. Therefore, cyborg insects must be produced stably and operate autonomously. In this study, the Madagascar hissing cockroach is used to control turning and straight movement by electrical stimulation of the antennae and cerci. In conventional methods, implanting electrodes into the antennae is a complicated and difficult procedure, which is an obstacle to stable production. The new method was proposed using a cylindricaljig with a horizontal hole and a needle piercing from the side of the antenna, realizing simple and stable electrode implantation. Furthermore, a cyborg insect developed using the proposed method was implemented for heat source approach control movement. It was shown that the cyborg insect could move autonomously based on the information from the onboard thermal imager and could move to the destination.

articleTitle: Acoustofluidic manipulation system with an open microfluidic chip
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we fabricated micromanipulation system based on an acoustofluidic phenomenon with an open microfluidic chip. Microfluidic chip is a strong candidate for manipulation of micro-and nanoparticles, but it is difficult to remove dust or bubbles from it because of its closed structure. By using an open chip, it becomes easy to remove dust or bubbles. In this study, we succeeded in constructing a system to manipulating particles by using open chip system with an acoustic radiation force.

articleTitle: Evaluation of pressure dispersion and limited photosensitization of cell membrane perforators with hollow geometry
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Recently, the control of cell function has attracted increasing attention, with the possibility of changing various morphological and functional forms of cells and organs. Cell modifications include virus vectors and lipofection methods; however, these approaches have limitations in terms of efficiency and process optimization. In contrast, our photochemical cell membrane perforation method exhibits high efficiency but requires a thermosetting silicone polymer-based cell membrane perforator as a consumable item, requiring a 4-h production time. Moreover, the success rate of cell perforation is low because of the application of uneven pressure on the cell population. In a previous study, we presented a process employing an injection-molding machine to manufacture thermoplastic elastomer-based perforators for mass production. This successfully shortened the production time to $\lt 1\mathrm{h}$ while preserving perforating function. Adopting a hollow shape to the perforator enabled the application of uniform pressure to the cell population. In addition, we successfully suppressed the unnecessary oxidative effects by limiting other photosensitizing functions. However, previous studies have not fully evaluated the perforation success rate by pressure dispersion of the cell population or by limiting the photosensitizing function. Therefore, in this study, we used human umbilical vein endothelial cells to introduce fluorescent substances and mRNA to evaluate the perforation success rate.

articleTitle: Micro-Scale Phase-separation Liposome Detection system of flavor concentrations in Sake, a traditional alcoholic drink in Japan
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Sake is a traditional Japanese alcoholic beverage containing ethyl caproate (EC) and isoamyl acetate (IA) flavoring agents to enhance its economic value. Isovaleraldehyde (IVA) is another well-known flavoring agent in alcoholic beverages which some people enjoy. Recent studies revealed that EC and IA decreased the size of homogenous 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3phosphocholine (DOPC) liposomes whereas IVA increased their size. The solid ordered/liquid disordered (Ld) and liquid ordered (Lo)/Ld phase separation in DOPC/dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3phosphocholine/cholesterol ternary membranes decreased after EC addition. Application aspects of EC evaluation were discussed. This study provides a rapid and cost-effective solution for the measurement.

articleTitle: Contact and Non-Contact Droplets Printing in Fluorocarbon (FC-40) with Automated 3D-Single Cell Printer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: High throughput screening, single-molecule analysis, single-cell analysis, cell culturing, microscale cell assay, and micro-sample analysis require 3D printing of nanoliter droplets. Droplets should be covered with fluorocarbons (FC-40) to avoid any kind of contamination with the environment and evaporation. Printing droplets in FC-40 is relatively difficult while following a 3D pattern for desired locations. The previous method of printing droplets needs a relatively large complex system size and high cost associated. To reduce the size and cost and fulfill the requirement, we demonstrated nL droplet printing in FC-40 by contact printing with an automated 3D-Single Cell printer. 3-Axis IAI Cartesian Robot and nano pass nozzle were prepared, and they are cheaper and easy to manufacture. The printed droplets kept their shape and position under the FC-40 until they evaporated. Droplets were printed at the desired locations and the size and volume of the droplets were controlled with a syringe pump and cartesian robots.

articleTitle: Cyborg Insects Powered by An Insect-Mountable Biofuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper describes the development of an electric stimulation device that can be driven by a biofuel cell (BFC) using insect hemolymph and the demonstration of locomotion control of insects with the electrical stimulator. The lifetime of batteries was one of the significant issues for the practical use of cyborg insects. In previous studies, coin batteries were used as the power source of electrical stimulators, but the operation time was around 1 hour. Hence, we previously reported an insect-mountable biofuel cell (imBFC) that can generate electric power from insect hemolymph and a radio sensor that can be driven by the imBFC. Because the imBFC uses blood sugar in insect hemolymph, the imBFC potentially offers a semi-permanent lifetime. Here, in this study, we developed an electrical stimulator that can be driven by the imBFC to develop a self-powered cyborg insect. The electrical stimulator consists of a power management IC with a voltage booster function and a microcontroller that generates electric stimulations. As a result, we successfully controlled the locomotion of insects using the imBFC-powered electrical stimulator. We believe that the self-powered cyborg insect will be applied for search and rescue missions at disaster sites.

articleTitle: Pre-training on physical dynamics enhances indirect sensing in recurrent neural networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMehatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: A McKibben-type pneumatic artificial muscle (PAM), which can achieve a large contraction force, is a promising candidate for the actuation of soft robots. Currently, to control PAMs, many sensors are required for controlling factors such as the length and internal pressure of the PAM, and the load applied to it. To reduce the weight and cost of soft robots and keep their characteristics intact, it is important to reduce the number of sensors as much as possible. In this study, we propose a machine learning scheme that can accurately predict PAM length using a small number of sensors. This is realized through the pre-training on the physical property of PAM in recurrent neural networks under the reservoir computing framework. First, we removed the load and length sensors and predicted the length of the PAM using only the internal pressure and electrical resistance sensors. The load applied to the PAM greatly affected its length, so the prediction accuracy was low, and the normalized mean square error (NMSE), which is an index of error, was NMSE =0.220. However, when the load was predicted from the internal pressure and electrical resistance, the load could be predicted with a high accuracy, and when self-feedback from this emulated load was added into the reservoir, the prediction accuracy of the length was greatly improved (NMSE =0.0330). In the end, we removed the load, length, and internal pressure sensors, and we predicted the length using only the electrical resistance sensor. The load and internal pressure were predicted from the electrical resistance, and these predicted values were fed back to the reservoir and used to predict the length. When the length was finally predicted, the prediction accuracy was higher than when it was predicted from just the electrical resistance. The mechanisms that supported this improvement and the role of feedback in the reservoir are discussed in detail.
